name.text: Shared: Identify the value of a digit by place value

questiontext.text:
Consider the number \[ {@number@}. \]

What is the value of the digit in the thousands place?

[[input:ans1]] [[validation:ans1]] [[feedback:prt1]]

generalfeedback.text:
Worked solution

The number is \[ {@number@}. \]

The digit in the thousands place is \[ {@thousands_digit@}. \]

A digit in the thousands place represents that digit multiplied by \(1000\). Therefore, \[ {@thousands_digit@}\times 1000 = {@answer@}. \]

So the value of the digit is \[ \boxed{{@answer@}}. \]

Learners identify the numerical value represented by a digit according to its position in a multi-digit whole number.

Distinguishes identifying a digit from identifying the value represented by that digit in its position.

Original STACK question. No source wording or mathematical content is copied.

Curriculum alignment is maintained outside the question source. This question may be mapped independently to Ghana, Kenya, or future curriculum profiles.

prtincorrect.text: That is not the value represented by the digit in that position.

node.description: Checks the positional value of the thousands digit.
Checks whether the learner entered only the digit instead of its positional value.

truefeedback.text:
You identified the correct digit, but the question asks for its value.

A digit in the thousands place represents that digit multiplied by \(1000\).

For example, a \(7\) in the thousands place represents \(7000\), not \(7\).

falsefeedback.text: Look at the position of the digit. The thousands place has a value of \(1000\) for each unit in that position.

qtest.description: Teacher answer should receive full credit.
Entering only the digit should be recognized as the targeted misconception.
